quotes.text: Latency isn't just a user experience problem. It's an adoption problem. If your employees try co-pilot twice, wait two seconds each time and decide it's faster to just do the work themselves, they won't come back.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Links model latency directly to Copilot adoption and ROI.

quotes.text: the sovereignty conversation can't end with Microsoft says it's compliant. It has to extend to can we verify and enforce compliance ourselves.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Clear stance that sovereignty requires verifiable control, not vendor assurances.

quotes.text: That's the wrong question. The right question is whether a small model can do the specific tasks you actually need and whether it can do them faster, cheaper and closer to your data.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Reframes how enterprises should evaluate small language models.

quotes.text: The key insight is that routing isn't an add-on, it's the architecture. Without it, you're either overpaying for frontier models on simple tasks or your underpowering complex tasks with small models.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: States the central architectural thesis of tiered model routing.

quotes.text: the goal is to stop using a single model for every task and instead build a portfolio where each model handles the work it was designed for
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the model mixture strategy in one sentence.

takeaways: Routing every Copilot request through a frontier model makes AI costly, slow and dependent on cloud processing locations you may not control.
Small language models such as Phi-3 handle the high-volume, narrow Microsoft 365 tasks like summarization, classification and drafting at a fraction of the cost and latency.
A tiered model mixture with policy and confidence-based routing, local deployment on Azure Local and clear governance lets organizations keep frontier models for the exceptions that need them.
hook: Copilot's real cost isn't the license but the frontier model behind every request, which drives up spend, slows responses and can process data outside the EU. This episode shows IT leaders and architects how small language models, tiered routing and local deployment on Azure Local make Copilot cheaper, faster and more sovereign.
